title: Help for Vendors Displaced by Closing of Sungei Road Hawking Zone
what_it_is: Help for Vendors Displaced by Closing of Sungei Road Hawking Zone

sections.label: Sungei Road vendors replacement and help
sections.summary: Questions ask whether the Government will reconsider a replacement site for Sungei Road Hawking Zone and for updates on help to vendors after closure.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether the Government will reconsider its decision not to provide a replacement site for the Sungei Road Hawking Zone (SRHZ); and (b) whether an update can be provided on the help given to the vendors and whether any additional help will be given to vendors after the closure of SRHZ.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources after the closure of the Sungei Road flea market, how will the Ministry engage and monitor the mental health of the elderly vendors who are displaced after losing their stalls and livelihood.

sections.label: Sungei Road closure date
sections.summary: The site is required by the Ministry of National Development for ground preparation works, so SRHZ's last day of operations will be 10 July 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This was also mentioned to this House in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Now that the site where SRHZ is located is required by the Ministry of National Development (MND) for ground preparation works to facilitate future public housing development, the last day of operations of SRHZ will be 10 July 2017.

sections.label: NEA stalls and rental rebates
sections.summary: NEA has set aside more than 40 lock-up stalls at hawker centres and offered the 11 original permit holders rental rebates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) has set aside more than 40 lock-up stalls at hawker centres for those SRHZ users who wish to carry on their trade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To assist them in their transition, we have offered the 11 original permit holders a 100% rental rebate for the first year and a 50% rental rebate for the second year.

sections.label: NEA, PA and CDC flea markets
sections.summary: NEA worked with the People's Association and Central Singapore CDC to help SRHZ users tap on existing flea markets, with 16 users applying for stalls.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To this end, NEA has worked with the People's Association (PA) and the Central Singapore Community Development Council (CDC) to assist the SRHZ users to tap on existing flea markets.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So far, 16 SRHZ users have applied for stalls at the flea markets at various locations, including those near their homes.

sections.label: MSF and CDC financial assistance
sections.summary: MSF and the Central Singapore CDC helped those needing financial assistance through ComCare and other schemes, with 18 of 23 applicants assessed eligible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MSF and the Central Singapore CDC have also been actively helping those who require financial assistance to get financial help through the ComCare scheme and other schemes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So far, 18 out of the 23 individuals who applied for financial assistance are assessed to be eligible and have received financial assistance.

sections.label: Vendors receiving Government assistance
sections.summary: More than 60 of them are now receiving some form of Government assistance, including those allocated stalls.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: More than 60 of them are now receiving some form of Government assistance, including those who have been allocated stalls.

sections.label: Transition help for relocated stallholders
sections.summary: Rental rebates, short training courses and information at SRHZ help ease relocated users into the transition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Regarding the first question, about how we can ensure that they succeed in the lock-up stalls in the hawker centres or markets or in the flea markets, as I have said earlier, we understand that in any change of business, for instance, business locations, a transition is required and it is not unexpected that business could be slow in the beginning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, to ease them into the transition, we have provided, as I have said, rental rebates as well as offer short training courses that will provide them with tips on merchandising, display and so on at the shops, as well as, of course, now we have put up information at the SRHZ itself to tell the customers there where some of these stalls or these users have relocated to.

sections.label: Engaging undecided users after closure
sections.summary: Users who decide only after SRHZ closes will still be engaged if they gave contact information.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to the 70 who have said that they will only decide after the closure of SRHZ, for those who have given us their contact information, we will continue to engage them even after the closure and see what kind of assistance they need.

sections.label: Relocation alternatives for SRHZ users
sections.summary: SRHZ users wanting to continue trading are offered relocation to lock-up stalls or existing flea markets.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: There are already existing avenues where such goods are sold, say, in the existing flea markets, which are also ground-up initiatives from the community mostly, and also online.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, in view of that, for SRHZ users who want to continue to ply the trade, we are offering them relocation alternatives, concrete relocation alternatives, either in lock-up stalls in the hawker centres and markets, or at existing flea markets where the goods sold are not incompatible with what the SRHZ users want to sell.

sections.label: Questions on elderly and livelihood users
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government's response to elderly needs and how many users depend on the zone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I wonder what is the Government's specific response to these needs, especially for the elderly?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Also, how many users has the Ministry found who are actually dependent on the zone for a livelihood?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Second, I would like to ask if the Ministry has analysed the reasons, as what my colleague Er Dr Lee has mentioned, and identified further solutions on how to address the grouses of poorer business by the current users who have moved or are going to move to lock-up stalls that are provided by NEA.

sections.label: Requests for replacement sites
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government's response to requests for replacement sites at free or low rent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Third, what is the Government's specific response to some of the requests of the users and supporters for relocations to several suggested replacement sites in the cities, or other preferred sites for free or very low rent with provision for storage space and shelter, and what is the Government's response if there are also other similar needs?

sections.label: Users not needing post-closure assistance
sections.summary: Of over 200 engaged users, more than 80 said they do not need assistance after SRHZ closes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Of the more than 200 that we have engaged, actually more than 80 have said that they do not need assistance after the closure of SRHZ.

sections.label: Lock-up stall allocations
sections.summary: 29 have been allocated lock-up stalls, including Mr Tang Kong Yuen, and 11 have started operating.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said, 29 have been allocated lock-up stalls, including Mr Tang Kong Yuen who is the Vice President of the Association for the Recycling of Second-hand Goods, and 11 of them have already started operating their lock-up stalls.

sections.label: Support for SRHZ users
sections.summary: Central CDC and Mayor Denise Phua helped SRHZ users with rental rebates, S&CC rebates and assistance schemes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Regarding the second question, which is quite similar to Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's question about how to ensure that they continue to be supported, first, let me place on record that we want to thank Mayor Denise Phua and the Central CDC for the tremendous help that her officers and herself have given during the last few months in engaging the SRHZ users, not just onsite, nearly every week onsite, but also offsite through phone calls, visits to the SRHZ users to see what kind of assistance could be rendered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I know that besides the assistance that we have given in terms of rental rebate, for instance, the service and conservancy charges rebates for two months as well as various other help that I have mentioned, the Central CDC has come up with various schemes to help them, including a transitional assistance programme and another new scheme that they are coming up with to help ensure or to help the SRHZ users at the lock-up stalls to give them a good chance to make sure that they can carry on their business there.
